notes: Perfect match on OxICAT methodology claims (C10, C11, C18, C19, C20). Both evaluators agree the technical approach is sound and well-validated.
High overlap on protective/beneficial role hypotheses (C77, C78, C81, C82, C83). Both evaluators agree these interpretations are speculative and require additional experimental validation.

Strong overlap on global redox collapse claims (C1, C25-C30, C33, C39, C44). Both agree the observational data on widespread protein oxidation is convincing and well-documented. Peer review includes additional claims (C6, C21, C76) also rated as supported.

Both address thioredoxin reductase genetic experiments (C57-C61). LLM rates UNSUPPORTED due to confounding factors preventing definitive conclusions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN and suggest additional experiments (weaker promoters, heterozygous diploids) are feasible, indicating they view the question as answerable rather than definitively unsupported.

Overlap on NADPH depletion observations (C3, C4, C65, C66, C69, C71). LLM rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of causal evidence and absence of direct ROS measurements. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal observations as convincing while separately noting causal limitations. Disagreement reflects different interpretation of what these specific claims assert (observation vs. mechanism).

Overlap on early oxidation targets and clustering analysis (C45, C50, C51, C54). Both agree the identification of early oxidation targets including thioredoxin reductase is methodologically sound and well-supported.

Overlap on caloric restriction effects (C5, C73, C99). Both accept the observational data showing CR delays NADPH depletion and oxidation while extending lifespan. LLM notes mechanistic interpretation is inferential but correlative evidence is strong; peer reviewers similarly accept temporal correlations.

Partial overlap on temporal relationship between oxidation and cell death (C6, C21, C26, C28, C30). Both agree the timeline showing oxidation precedes death by 3-4 days is well-established. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader redox collapse assessment.
Overlap on ATP maintenance despite oxidation (C41, C42, C43). Both agree the metabolic data showing maintained energy resources is convincing and well-supported.
Overlap on identification of oxidized proteins in translation/metabolism (C34, C35, C36). Both accept the proteome-wide identification and clustering analysis as thorough and convincing.

Overlap on causal mechanism claims (C2, C96, C98). LLM rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct NADPH manipulation and ROS measurements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting conclusions are limited without direct testing of whether NADPH depletion causes aging. Both agree causality is not established.

Minimal overlap on reversibility experiments (C55, C56). Both support these claims, but LLM R4 focuses on broader early oxidation targets while peer R11 emphasizes GapDH and reversibility data specifically.

Minimal overlap on redox-sensitive cysteines (C31, C32). Both support these claims but group them differently. LLM R1 includes in global collapse assessment; peer R11 focuses on GapDH and reversibility.
Minimal overlap (C29, C30) on temporal dynamics. Both support these claims but in different contexts. LLM R3 addresses CR effects; peer R1 addresses global redox collapse.

Minimal overlap on clustering analysis (C48). Both support the clustering methodology but focus on different aspects. LLM R4 emphasizes early targets; peer R12 focuses on aromatic amino acid enrichment.

Minimal overlap (C51 only). LLM rates genetic experiments UNSUPPORTED due to confounding factors. Peer R5 rates identification of thioredoxin reductase as early target SUPPORTED, focusing on observational clustering rather than genetic perturbation. Disagreement reflects different claim scope.
Minimal overlap (C70). Both support NADPH-related observations but in different contexts. LLM R3 addresses CR effects; peer R2 addresses temporal NADPH depletion.
Minimal overlap (C46). Both support clustering analysis claims but group differently. LLM R1 includes in global collapse; peer R12 focuses on sequence analysis.
Minimal overlap (C76). Both support claims about oxidized proteins and cell viability but in different groupings. Agreement on the underlying data quality.
